## Work tracking
Use the live **status:**, **priority:** and **complexity:** labels above; **Assignees** identifies the owner. These labels are separate from the task/ticket type.

**Planning complexity:** XL - Umbrella delivery spanning the full product; execute through child tasks, not as one work item.
Complexity is a provisional scope/uncertainty estimate, not a delivery-time commitment. XL work must be split into executable subtasks before starting.
**Planning priority:** P0 - Architecture/foundation work that unblocks the implementation path.

### Live views
- [Your Project #6 board](https://github.com/orgs/Do-Zu/projects/6)
- [Doing](https://github.com/Do-Zu/dozu/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20is%3Aopen%20label%3A%22status%3Ain-progress%22) | [Review](https://github.com/Do-Zu/dozu/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20is%3Aopen%20label%3A%22status%3Ain-review%22) | [Ready](https://github.com/Do-Zu/dozu/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20is%3Aopen%20label%3A%22status%3Aready%22)
- [Blocked](https://github.com/Do-Zu/dozu/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20is%3Aopen%20label%3A%22status%3Ablocked%22) | [Waiting on prerequisites](https://github.com/Do-Zu/dozu/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20is%3Aopen%20label%3A%22status%3Awaiting%22)

### Workflow rules
Keep exactly one status, priority and complexity label per issue. Assign an owner when work starts. Waiting means ordinary dependencies remain; blocked requires a specific reason. Close as completed only after acceptance evidence/review; a closed-not-planned item is not done. Start no more than one issue per owner unless deliberately agreed. Your main board is [Dozu Project #6](https://github.com/orgs/Do-Zu/projects/6). Issue labels and project fields are initialized consistently, but no automatic two-way synchronization is configured. Built-in Labels and Assignees reflect their issues; custom project Status/Priority/Complexity must be maintained deliberately. Local dashboard counts are snapshots refreshed by sync-issue-tracking.ps1.

Priority: P0 architecture/foundation unblockers; P1 required feature/integration/release work; P2 required supporting work later in the sequence; P3 optional/future only if explicitly added. Complexity: S contained; M moderate; L cross-system/native/security; XL umbrella/high uncertainty requiring breakdown.

## Accepted desktop resource contract — 2026-11-14

Authority: the user explicitly accepted the proposed larger initial-release hardware/resource targets in the #8 chat. OS versions, CPU architecture matrix, installer formats, feature/data/security/lifecycle obligations and deferred capabilities are unchanged. Requirements approval is not benchmark or release acceptance.

| Hardware | Minimum | Recommended |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CPU | 64-bit, 4 physical cores | 6–8 cores |
| System RAM | 8 GB | 16 GB |
| Storage | SSD; 10 GB free before installation | SSD; 20 GB free |
| Graphics | Integrated graphics; CPU inference | Dedicated GPU optional |
| Display | 1366 × 768 | 1920 × 1080 |

| Initial-release whole-application target | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Installer download | ≤ 1.5 GB |
| Installed application, all bundled runtimes/model/resources included | ≤ 3 GB |
| Normal combined app memory | ≤ 2 GB RAM |
| Peak during one ingestion/embedding job | ≤ 3 GB RAM |
| Interactive UI after cold launch | ≤ 15 s |
| Complete local backend/model readiness | ≤ 30 s |

Memory includes Electron, Next, Express, PostgreSQL, Redis and running embedding/conversion workers. The existing warm-UI targets were not changed: ≤5 s on minimum and ≤3 s on recommended hardware. Imported documents/media, growing databases and user backups require additional disk. Installation/update/restore preflight must calculate actual staging and data requirements rather than assuming the initial free-space allowance covers unlimited data.

Keep the existing pinned multilingual CPU model for the initial integration path; smaller/quantized runtime optimization may follow later. ONNX is an evaluation candidate, not a release prerequisite or an approved model substitution. Preserve real semantic PDF/YouTube transcript references, the 384-dimensional API contract, English/Vietnamese behavior, local authority and genuine provider integrations. No STT, SMTP, payment execution or pgvector is restored by this amendment; Redis and PostgreSQL remain retained.

Minimum-hardware acceptance uses one active user with one ingestion job at a time; concurrent LAN hosting and large-library capacity require separate measured tests. Validate the complete application on actual 8 GB/four-core SSD hardware and every required native OS/architecture before advertising support. Component proof, larger allowances and approval do not pass installer, full-stack memory/startup, native dependency, file-path/ownership or lifecycle ACs.

Canonical requirements and evidence rules: [platform-support.md](https://github.com/Do-Zu/dozu/blob/dev/planning/platform-support.md). Prior measurements and closed issue histories remain historical evidence; no completed/cancelled issue is reopened or counted as release proof by this change.

## Outcome
Package the complete existing website, backend and local data stack for Windows, macOS and Linux. Internet-enabled third-party features remain genuine integrations. Each user's computer is the primary source of truth.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Next.js frontend, Express/business logic, PostgreSQL, local files/jobs and FastAPI run on the user's machine without manual runtime/database setup.
- [ ] Preserve ALL pages, layouts, components, navigation, roles, locales and features; retain the website build and a localhost browser interface using the same local backend.
- [ ] Google/YouTube/email/payments/AI/classroom integration limitations have verified desktop-compatible designs; no online feature is silently removed or replaced with a simulation.
- [ ] Application data, accounts, progress, settings, jobs and uploads remain local; no required central Dozu service, cloud database or synchronization.
- [ ] Clean-machine installation, restart/crash recovery, upgrade/backup/restore, complete feature parity and uninstall keep/delete options pass on every supported platform.

## Architecture constraints
The complete existing Next.js UI and Express backend run locally with a local database/files. Desktop and local browser use the same localhost backend. Real third-party integrations may use the internet; preserve them wherever feasible. No central Dozu backend, cloud database, synchronization, shared publisher secrets in installers, or simulated replacements. All existing pages remain in scope; explicit v1 capability deferrals in the 2026-11-11 amendment below apply.

## Authoritative requirement update
The user's latest clarification requires a self-hosted, local-first desktop with optional internet connectivity. It supersedes both earlier remote-backend and fully air-gapped assumptions. Third-party APIs are allowed; the application backend and authoritative storage remain local.

## Recommended stack
Electron + TypeScript supervising the existing Next.js standalone app, existing Express API, bundled PostgreSQL, durable local jobs/cache adapters, and bundled FastAPI/embedding model. Preserve external AI provider interfaces with scoped user-owned credentials. pnpm workspaces/Turborepo + uv for development/build tooling.

## Repository
```text
apps/web                 complete current Next.js app
apps/api                 existing Express, local/website runtime profiles
apps/desktop             Electron shell, supervisor, installer hooks
services/embedding       bundled FastAPI service
packages/local-runtime   local bootstrap/jobs/files/cache/provider adapters
packages/runtime-contracts
resources/manifests      binaries/models/assets/license/checksum manifests
infra/                   dev tooling + retained website deployment
docs/                    architecture/integrations/release evidence
```

## Runtime
Electron/local browser → local Next.js → localhost Express → local PostgreSQL/files/jobs/FastAPI. Express may call third-party Google, YouTube, SMTP, payments and configured AI providers when requested. Backend code is shared; every desktop installation owns its own backend instance and database.

## Release sequence
Requirements/integration audit → monorepo and packaged runtime proof → local providers and real integration adaptation → complete UI/feature parity → signed installers, data lifecycle and release evidence. The early proof is not a reduced-feature release.

## Specific limits to resolve
Desktop apps cannot protect a shared publisher merchant/API/SMTP secret. Use native public clients, user-owned credentials or supported provider delegation. Webhooks cannot target 127.0.0.1; verify authenticated outbound reconciliation or an opt-in scoped public callback/tunnel when required. Separate classroom installations do not share state without an explicit reachable host; no cloud sync is proposed.

- [Electron process supervision](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/utility-process)
- [Google desktop OAuth](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/native-app)
- [PayOS API](https://payos.vn/docs/api/)
- [Electron security](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/security)

## User-approved v1 decisions — 2026-11-10

The user has supplied the v1 support contract. This supersedes the earlier pending-decision note. These are requirements and engineering targets, not measured results.

## OS, architecture and distribution

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Windows | Windows 10 22H2, legacy compatibility; Windows 11, primary | x86-64 | NSIS .exe primary; .msi optional for enterprise |
| macOS | macOS 13 Ventura or later | Intel x86-64 and Apple Silicon ARM64 | Signed and notarized .dmg for each architecture |
| Linux | Ubuntu 22.04 LTS and Debian 12 minimum tested baselines; Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or newer recommended | x86-64 | .deb for Ubuntu/Debian; additional .AppImage where compatible |

32-bit systems are unsupported. Windows ARM64 and Linux ARM64 may be added only after native dependency validation; they are not current required v1 targets. Later recommended releases still require compatibility evidence; the wording above does not assert tests have run.

## Hardware

| Configuration | CPU | System RAM | Free disk | Display / storage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Minimum | 64-bit, 4 physical cores | 8 GB | 10 GB free before installation | 1366 × 768; integrated graphics; SSD required |
| Recommended | 6–8 cores | 16 GB | 20 GB free | 1920 × 1080; SSD |

A dedicated GPU is not required; retained embeddings run on CPU. The 8 GB/four-core minimum is an accepted validation target and is not yet a verified support claim. Use one active user and at most one ingestion/embedding job at a time for minimum-device acceptance, with bounded batches/caches and controlled background concurrency. Concurrent LAN hosts and large libraries require separate capacity measurements; their workflows remain in scope. The earlier 4 GB/HDD minimum and 4 GB low-resource acceptance target are superseded. Preserve functionality while optimizing later.

## Performance and disk targets

| Production-build metric | Minimum-spec device | Recommended device |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cold launch to interactive UI | ≤ 15 s | ≤ 15 s |
| Warm launch to interactive UI | ≤ 5 s | ≤ 3 s |
| Complete local backend/model ready | ≤ 30 s | ≤ 30 s |
| Normal combined application memory | ≤ 2 GB | ≤ 2 GB |
| Combined peak during one ingestion/embedding job | ≤ 3 GB | ≤ 3 GB |

Installer download target: **≤ 1.5 GB**. Installed application target: **≤ 3 GB**, including all bundled frontend/backend/database/cache runtimes, model and processing resources, attribution and verification metadata. Require **at least 10 GB free before installation**; 20 GB is recommended. Imported documents/media, growing databases and user backups require additional storage. Account for every shipped runtime/model/asset; no first-run runtime/model download or relabeling installed resources as user data. Installer/upgrade/restore preflight must calculate actual staging/data needs; initial free-space allowances are not unlimited upgrade or backup guarantees. GB/MB values use decimal bytes in evidence comparisons.

Use production builds and documented repeatable workloads on actual 8 GB/four-core SSD minimum configurations. Document OS/CPU/RAM/storage, dataset/media sizes, model revision, cache state, concurrency, network state and measurement method. Report all app-owned processes, including Electron, Next, Express, PostgreSQL, Redis and running embedding/conversion workers, with shared-memory accounting documented. Separate interactive-UI and complete backend/model readiness; an interactive shell is not proof the services/model are ready. Measure normal, background and one-job processing peaks against the 2 GB/3 GB combined targets. Warm-UI targets remain ≤5 s minimum/≤3 s recommended because the user did not revise them. No numerical CPU utilization cap or fixed peak upgrade-space budget was agreed; measure them and validate disk preflight.

## Local runtime and data lifecycle

Backend and primary data storage run locally. Internet is permitted for genuine Google authentication, email, YouTube and other external services; classroom v1 is LAN, and payments are explicitly deferred/blocked under #41. No externally hosted application backend is required for core local functionality. Bundle/provision required dependencies through installation; no manual Node, Python, database, Docker, WSL or developer tooling. Retain the earlier self-contained baseline model/runtime requirement.

PostgreSQL/pgvector remains the source-supported candidate. The user permits considering SQLite **only after compatibility with the existing backend/business requirements is validated**. This does not authorize a database replacement: #4/#29 must prove migrations, PostgreSQL-specific SQL/JSONB, vector(384)/cosine/HNSW behavior and repository contracts before recommending an alternative.

Upgrades preserve data. Uninstall retains the earlier explicit keep-data/delete-all-app-owned-data choice, with reliable removal of app-owned databases, caches, logs and local data while protecting unrelated files. All managed data stays on the device unless the feature explicitly requires external communication. LAN participants access the user-owned host's authoritative data; no cloud database/sync is introduced.

## Evidence gates

#4/#38 must prove each agreed native OS/CPU combination and resource budget; #21/#32 include all media/conversion/transcription/model/font/browser resources discovered by audit. Electron + Next + Express + PostgreSQL + Python/model and conversion resources have not yet been shown to fit these budgets. No target is relaxed based on that uncertainty.

#22/#23/#25/#33/#35/#36 validate clean installation, startup/readiness, memory/core functionality, dependency compatibility, low-resource mode, restart/recovery, upgrades/backup/restore and uninstall on the minimum configurations. Release compliance requires actual evidence. Signing/distribution remain #24/#26. A benchmark failure requires evidence and an explicit recommendation before changing this contract.


Payment decision: explicitly defer/skip payment execution and retain existing issue #41 as the single blocker. Merchant ownership is deferred, not selected. Preserve page/history inventory and a clear disabled/unavailable payment state when implemented; no live charges, fake success or payment-page deletion. This is an explicit scope exception to earlier all-feature wording.

Classroom decision: other devices on the same LAN use a user-owned authoritative local host. Preserve teacher/student workflows with explicit LAN access/auth/TLS/availability proof under #43. Remote internet/tunnel participants are not a v1 requirement. No central Dozu backend/cloud database/sync.

All five #2 criteria are now evidenced as requirements. Implementation, installer/platform compatibility, performance/resource benchmarks, provider flows, data lifecycle and LAN runtime proof remain open under downstream issues. Source trees remain unchanged.

## User-approved v1 scope amendment — 2026-11-11

- Remove local speech-to-text from this version: no whisper.cpp server, tiny speech model, speech startup/readiness gate or speech-only assets. Retain independent media playback and genuine existing YouTube transcript text retrieval. Preserve source/page inventory; no fake transcript or new cloud STT fallback.
- Keep PostgreSQL; **defer pgvector**. A private relational cluster, reviewed migrations/seeds, persistence and data-safe upgrades remain required. - The measured 479.729 MB MiniLM snapshot is a separate **text-embedding model**, used by retained PDF/YouTube reference search and ingestion. Semantic reference retrieval has not been deferred by this decision.
- Exclude FFmpeg only when its sole consumer is deferred speech-to-text; separately prove any retained non-STT need. Keep required document/URL/PDF/editor/media/font/browser resources.
